calls.body: The Maple Leafs’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Islanders’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Islanders more than most.

calls.head: Active D vs. Forward-led
calls.body: The Islanders’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Maple Leafs’ not so much. The Islanders are the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Islanders’ defensemen jump into the play.

surprises.head: Ilya Sorokin stole one
surprises.body: Sorokin allowed 1 goal on 29 shots, worth 3.5 expected goals: 2.5 fewer than expected. That is more than the Islanders’ winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 30 starts.

surprises.head: Toronto got the good looks
surprises.body: Toronto’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.0% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Sorokin stands on his head
paras: The Islanders’ Calum Ritchie left early in the first period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was ruled out for 4-6 weeks with a lower-body injury. Anthony Duclair got the scoring started for the Islanders midway through the period. The Islanders’ Matias Maccelli left late in the period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was ruled out for 4-6 weeks with a lower-body injury. Bo Horvat made it 2-0 for the Isles late in the second. Colton Sissons pulled the Maple Leafs within one early in the third, but that was as close as they got. Simon Holmström stretched the lead to 3-1 with just under six minutes left, and he struck again into the empty net with just over two minutes left.

The score flatters the Islanders: the Maple Leafs had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Maple Leafs win about six in ten. Ilya Sorokin was the difference, stopping 28 of 29. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 16 of 19 for the Maple Leafs. The Islanders moved to 4-3-1 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Maple Leafs fell to 3-4-2, sinking to the bottom of the Atlantic.
